articles.title: Critical Drupal RCE Vulnerability Could Let Attackers Take Over Websites Without Authentication
articles.summary:
Drupal has released security updates for a critical remote code execution vulnerability that could let attackers take over affected websites without logging in. Tracked as CVE-2026-108097, the flaw affects the Field UI module in Drupal core. The Drupal Security Team published its warning on October 14, 2026. The official security advisory, SA-CORE-2026-014, assigns the issue […]

articles.title: Microsoft Says AI Agents Cannot Be Trusted and Could Become Insider Security Threats
articles.summary:
Microsoft warns organizations to treat AI agents as potential insider risks not because they are automatically malicious, but because they can access company data, apps, and tools and act on that access at high speed. The warning, published on October 19, 2026, comes as businesses use agents to handle tasks such as writing code, reviewing […]

articles.title: NSA, CISA and NIST Release New Security Guidelines to Detect and Shut Down Rogue AI Agents
articles.summary:

articles.title: Hackers Exploit SiteGuard WAF Vulnerability That Could Give Them Full Control of Servers
articles.summary:
Hackers are exploiting a command injection flaw in SiteGuard Server Edition, a web application firewall installed directly on protected servers. Tracked as CVE-2026-106931, the vulnerability could let attackers run operating system commands with root or SYSTEM privileges, potentially giving them full control of an affected server. articles.title: Hackers Registered New Teams-Based Domains and Used a Login Page to Steal Your Logins
articles.summary:
A newly registered domain copies Microsoft Teams’ login page and interface, raising concerns about a phishing attempt targeting workplace users. Security researcher Steven Lim reported that teams-cloud[.]live was just five days old when he flagged it on October 18, 2026. He urged organizations to block the address before employees encounter the fake site. The alert […]

articles.title: 16-Year-Old Broadcom Wi-Fi Flaw Lets Attackers Hack Routers Without Knowing Passwords
articles.summary:
A 16-year-old flaw in Broadcom’s Wi-Fi software can let attackers within wireless range take control of affected routers without knowing the network password. Security researcher Quentin Kaiser disclosed the issue at Hexacon in Paris on October 16, 2026, warning that old code remains in widely deployed devices.
